related_questions.question: Does the Moderna vaccine cause increased heart rate?

text_blocks.snippet: While some individuals may experience a temporary increase in heart rate after receiving the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine, it's generally not a common or severe side effect. Palpitations or changes in heart rhythm have been reported, but these are typically mild and temporary.
snippet_highlighted_words: some individuals may experience a temporary increase in heart rate after receiving the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine, it's generally not a common or severe side effect

list.title: Temporary increase in heart rate:
list.snippet: Some people may notice their heart beating faster than usual shortly after vaccination, but this usually subsides quickly.

list.title: Palpitations:
list.snippet: There have been reports of palpitations (a feeling of fluttering or pounding heart) following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, including the Moderna vaccine.

list.title: Arrhythmias:
list.snippet: In rare cases, heart rhythm disorders (arrhythmias) have been reported after vaccination.

list.title: Likely temporary and mild:
list.snippet: The vast majority of reported cases of increased heart rate or palpitations are mild and resolve on their own without specific treatment.

list.title: Not a common side effect:
list.snippet: While these side effects can occur, they are not widespread among vaccinated individuals.

list.title: No strong link to natural progression of heart conditions:
list.snippet: One study found that the increase in heart rhythm issues after vaccination was likely due to the natural progression of heart conditions rather than being directly caused by the vaccine.
